gaps.sentence: Local residents are deeply ___ about the new motorway plan.
gaps.explanation: deeply concerned is the standard collocation meaning very worried; the other adjectives do not collocate with 'deeply'.

gaps.sentence: The children were told not to ___ so much noise.
gaps.explanation: make a noise / make noise is the fixed collocation.

gaps.sentence: He was exhausted because he had ___ the cooking for twenty people.
gaps.explanation: do the cooking is the fixed phrase; after 'had' the past participle 'done' is needed.

gaps.sentence: The company ___ losses of two million last year.
He ___ a fortune selling software online.
gaps.explanation: make a fortune means to earn a very large amount of money.

gaps.sentence: All candidates must ___ the written exam in June.
gaps.hint: collocation with 'exam' from the candidate's side
gaps.explanation: take an exam (or sit an exam) means to be tested; 'give an exam' is not used in British English.

gaps.sentence: She ___ no difficulty finding the address.
gaps.hint: fixed pattern: ___ no difficulty doing something
gaps.explanation: have no difficulty (in) doing something is the fixed pattern; 'made no difficulty' is wrong.

gaps.sentence: Wrap up warm, or you'll ___ a cold.
gaps.explanation: catch a cold is the fixed collocation for becoming ill with one.
